item.title: “Get Julian Sayin Out of Columbus”: Fans React as OSU QB’s Interception Puts Buckeyes in Trouble vs Indiana
item.description: Ohio State Buckeyes quarterback Julian Sayin (10) runs during the first half of the NCAA football game against the Texas Longhorns at Ohio Stadium on Aug. 30, 2025. Credit: Imagn Last season, the Indiana Hoosiers snapped Ohio State’s winning streak, and as the two teams meet for the first time since, Julian Sayin and company have a chance to renew their matchup. However, in the second quarter, Sayin tried to pass to Jeremiah Smith, but Amare Ferrell intercepted it, which eventually led to an Indiana touchdown. Soon enough, Ohio State fans took to social media and slammed Sayin, with many calling out the quarterback. “Get Julian Sayin out of Columbus, man,” said one Ohio State fan. After intercepting Julian Sayin, Amare Ferrell had a 23-yard return for Indiana. This eventually led to a 7-yard rushing touchdown from Turbo Richard, giving the Hoosiers the lead with 13:54 remaining in the second quarter. A few minutes later, Sayin had another chance to connect with Jeremiah Smith, who actually beat the double coverage this time. The catch was still contested, with the quarterback missing the throw. This forced Ohio State to try to score another field goal, but the team failed. Nick Saban Says To Stop Jeremiah Smith, Indiana Must Stop Julian Sayin So far, Jeremiah Smith has been the favorite to win the Heisman this year, and this is all thanks to him playing well with quarterback Julian Sayin. Ahead of the game, on “College GameDay,” former Alabama coach and ESPN analyst Nick Saban said that to stop Jeremiah Smith, one must stop Julian Sayin. “I think the best way to slow down Jeremiah Smith is to affect the quarterback, and that’s the one thing Ohio State’s going to have to do today: They’re going to have to handle Indiana’s pressure,” Saban said. “Julian Sayin has been affected by pressure. His completion percentage goes down to 56%. Indiana has 49 tackles for loss, so they’re good at getting you behind the sticks, and they have 20 sacks, which is among the top in the country.” With seven national championships, Nick Saban knows a thing or two about stopping an opponent’s star player, and so far, Indiana has been handling Julian Sayin. item.title: Why Alex de Minaur’s Grand Slam dream may be further away than ever after latest statistic emerges
item.description: Alex de Minaur is one of the most likeable players on the ATP Tour, and he makes it so easy to root for him. After all, he boasts a work ethic that demands admiration, and an upbeat personality that continues to win fans. However, for all his effort and application, at the Grand Slam level, it feels as though he remains wanting. The Australian is a seven-time major quarter-finalist, having never made it further than that stage. As impressive as he can be at these events, the barrier is clear. And, what’s even more worrying is a recent statistic that has emerged, which makes his Grand Slam dream only feel further away. Alex de Minaur’s worrying record against the best players on the ATP Tour Realistically, if Alex de Minaur is to break past his current quarter-final hoodoo, or even go all the way, he will likely have to defeat one of Carlos Alcaraz, Jannik Sinner, Novak Djokovic or Alexander Zverev. However, his record against all four makes for rather dire reading, especially when excluding team events like the ATP Cup, United Cup, and the Davis Cup. If those results are removed, the 27-year-old has never beaten any of this elite quartet, losing all 29 meetings. His aspiration for the majors is clear, and De Minaur has not been shy in voicing it either. Viewing a statistic as damning as this does make it hard to imagine him ever surpassing that quarter-final block, especially given his inability to capitalise at this year’s Roland Garros or Wimbledon events, where Alcaraz was absent from both, and Sinner and Djokovic both lost early in Paris. Despite his dire combined record, De Minaur retains his patented positivity, even if it has felt like more and more negativity has been creeping into some of his post-match assessments. item.title: “Julian Sayin Allergic to Throwing to Jeremiah Smith”: Fans React as Indiana Shuts Down OSU WR in 1H with “Calvin Johnson” Coverage
item.description: Wide receiver Jeremiah Smith. © IMAGN Indiana appeared to use extra coverage while facing Ohio State star wide receiver Jeremiah Smith on Saturday. Known for his explosive plays, Smith is not getting an easy one-on-one matchup against the national champions. Analyst Pat McAfee noted similarities between how Smith was defended and how Calvin Johnson was defended back in the day. Johnson, nicknamed “Megatron,” was one of the NFL’s most physically imposing receivers. Smith has drawn similar comparisons after two Indiana defenders appeared to be near him. “We’re getting REAL close to the Calvin Johnson punt gunner coverage for Jeremiah Smith,” McAfee wrote. Fans shared their reactions to Indiana’s strategy to stop Ohio State quarterback Julian Sayin from getting easy access to one of the best wide receivers in college. “Sayin allergic to throwing to Jeremiah Smith,” one fan wrote. “No other WR gets covered like this in college football,” one fan noted. “Stop insulting Calvin’s dominance. Jeremiah Smith isn’t that,” one fan remarked. “Always a legend,” one fan wrote. “No joke, Pat, at this point I don’t think press with two over him in addition is off the table. Use 3,” one fan said. “Jeremiah Smith gets the Shaq treatment. They simply won’t call PI by smaller DB,” one fan compared the receiver to an NBA legend. Indiana Gets Concerning Jeremiah Smith Prediction Ahead of Ohio State Showdown Jeremiah Smith is easily one of the best receivers in college football this season. The Ohio State Buckeyes receiver entered Saturday’s game with 916 receiving yards and 11 touchdowns in six games this season. Despite Indiana’s unbeaten 6-0 start this season, NBC analyst Todd Blackledge believes the Hoosiers won’t be able to stop Smith on the field. “Another issue where I think, and this will show itself, you know, how they’re going to deal with Jeremiah Smith, they’re not as good in the boundary corner as they were last year with D’Angelo Ponds,” Blackledge said. “I mean, they felt like he could really, they could count on him to do what he needed to do, lock something down, they could be creative and cover each other places with their simulated pressures and all of that.” So far in the first two quarters, Indiana’s strategy might be working because Sayin hasn’t thrown a lot to Smith in the first half despite Ohio State trailing 7-3 at the end of the second quarter. He has two receptions for 20 yards. item.title: Angel Reese reveals her immediate plan after Dream’s WNBA Finals Game 1 loss to Valkyries
item.description: Kelley L Cox-Imagn Images Angel Reese reveals her immediate plan after Dream’s WNBA Finals Game 1 loss to Valkyries appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Game 1 of the WNBA Finals was highly competitive, but the Golden State Valkyries emerged victorious over the Atlanta Dream with a 68-64 win. Gabby Williams led the way for Golden State with 26 points, while Allisha Gray — who was questionable to play before being made available — had 19 points for Atlanta. Meanwhile, Angel Reese turned in a strong 14-point, 12-rebound double-double. After the game, Reese revealed what she is planning on doing following the defeat, via Winsidr. “Yeah, just going back into the film room and figuring out things that we messed up on, things that we can be better at,” Reese told reporters. Reese had a quiet second half following a big first half. When asked about that after the game, Reese said she simply wasn’t aggressive enough from an offensive standpoint, via ClutchPoints. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “I don’t think they (Valkyries) really did anything (to slow her down in the second half). Maybe that was just on me,” Reese said. “I wasn’t aggressive enough with the ball… So, definitely going to do a better job of that next game.” The Dream still kept things competitive on the road. item.title: Dodgers fan favorite acknowledges potential final season with LA in message: ‘If this is it for us’
item.description: Kiké Hernandez may have played his final game with the Dodgers. The fan favorite acknowledged the uncertain future he faces as he enters free agency in an Instagram post in which Hernandez expressed his gratefulness for fans. Los Angeles Dodgers’ Kike Hernandez gestures toward his dugout after hitting a two-run home run during the seventh inning of a baseball game against the Cincinnati Reds, Wednesday, Sept. 9, 2026, in Los Angeles. AP Photo/Mark J. Terrill “LA, we fell short of our big goal. But looking at the big picture, what a ride these last three years were!!” Hernandez wrote in the Instagram caption. “If this is it for us…. Once again, I will always be thankful for you guys & I will forever love ya! #JustAKidFromPR,” Hernandez said. President of baseball operations Andrew Friedman brought Hernandez back on a one-year deal last offseason, saying the “door was always open” for the utilityman. It remains unclear whether that will be the case this winter as Hernandez hits free agency again. Hernandez has built his career as an electric personality in the Dodgers’ dugout and a clutch bat every October. His postseason numbers are simply mystifying with Hernandez coming to life every fall. Kike Hernandez #8 of the Los Angeles Dodgers in the dugout during the game against the Colorado Rockies Getty Images But as the Dodgers look to get younger, the front office may go in another direction this offseason. The Dodgers assembled the most expensive roster in baseball, which also happened to be the oldest. While the Dodgers won 100 regular-season games with their veteran core, the back-to-back World Series champions were swept by a hungrier, younger Brewers team. Hernandez, who has been a key part of Los Angeles’ back-to-back World Series titles, could play another major role in the postseason. Getty Images The four-game sweep in the National League Championship Series may alter the Dodgers’ plans as the front office attempts to build another winning roster. Only time will tell whether Hernandez is a part of that group.

Credit to Wardley for surviving the initial knockdown which would have dropped a rhino, and the next five minutes of the fight. Outside a boxing ring, Dubois would be charged with aggravated assault. Wardley’s trainer Ben Davison admitted a few days after the first fight that he made a mistake not stepping in earlier. He was on the top step near the end of the first round with the towel in his hand, but Wardley got out of the first round. Referee Steve Gray had nerves of steel in not stopping the fight himself at any point in the first round. Wardley didn’t have enough time in the corner to recover. The damage left from the first fight emerged as the second round ticked by. Finally, Davison did the right thing and the towel came into the ring. Dubois: “I Had Bad Intentions” Daniel Dubois came in focused with only one outcome in mind: a more significant victory than in the first fight. Photo: Queensberry Promotions “I had bad intentions from the beginning, and this is God’s victory tonight, and we done we done well,” said Dubois. “This time, we just had to go out there and show that we mean business, and that’s what we did tonight.” Wardley: “The Game Is The Game” Wardley made no excuses for the outcome in the rematch, but vowed it wasn’t the end. “Look, it’s never fun to lose, but it is what it is. Photo: Queensberry Promotions The analysis immediately turned to whether Wardley rushed the rematch after taking tremendous punishment from Dubois in the first fight. Wardley disagreed. “Not at all. Look, I just came in. I didn’t execute the game plan properly tonight. That was all. I hold my hands up to that. It’s entirely down to me,” explained Wardley. Wardley also absolved his team, including head trainer Ben Davison, who’s now seen two of his three heavyweight stars, Dubois and Moses Itauma, take losses. “When I step through the ropes, it’s only myself. It’s only me and me bouncing around in the ring and doing everything. There’s no blame to be passed around. When I win, it’s all me as well. So, look, we’ll go back to the drawing board as a team. There’s no shame in losing to a great competitor like Daniel.” The Heavyweight Division Outlook It will be wise for Wardley to sit out for a longer spell, reassess and put in some months in the gym in 2027 before coming back. Queensberry Promotions and Frank Warren will welcome him with open arms. Wardley is likeable, popular, and easy to work with. With Agit Kabayel vs Nelson Hysa ticket sales now well over 42,000, let’s see if Croatia’s enthusiasm catch match it. As the Los Angeles Dodgers were swept by the Milwaukee Brewers in the NLCS, the team now moves on to the offseason, where there are decisions to be made about which players to bring back. Essentially, they’ve been missing their entire second line for five games and depth guys were being asked to punch well above their weight class. item.title: Instant reactions to Alabama's ugly road loss vs. Tennessee
item.description: On Saturday afternoon, the Alabama Crimson Tide traveled for the latest chapter of the Third Saturday in October at Neyland Stadium, a venue that has given the program fits in recent trips . One of the SEC's most storied rivalries, it was eventually more of the same for Alabama on Saturday afternoon. The Crimson Tide were plagued by a slow start offensively, and went on to struggle mightily in a number of different areas. As a result, Alabama suffered yet another road loss to Tennessee in a game where they never led , 26-10. A game that simply did not feature a lot of positives for the Crimson Tide, let's take a look at some instant reactions to Alabama's latest loss in Neyland Stadium. Alabama has ugly offensive showing To keep it simple, this was likely one of the worst offensive showings we have seen from Alabama in recent memory. The Crimson Tide could not get anything going at any point during the game, finishing with only 201 yards of total offense. Alabama also committed four turnovers, and struggled mightily on third down by going 2-of-13, as well as 1-of-3 on fourth down. The Crimson Tide also had only seven first downs the entire game. Alabama's rough start in first half While the offense struggled the entire game, Alabama really put themselves in a hole early with a rough showing in the first half. At halftime, Alabama trailed 12-10 following an offensive half that included only 93 total yards, three turnovers, and a combined 0-of-8 on third-and-fourth downs. Alabama loses the line of scrimmage A major storyline coming in, Alabama lost the line of scrimmage on both sides of the ball Saturday afternoon. The Crimson Tide offensive line gave up five sacks to only one for Alabama's defense, while the Volunteers also out-rushed Alabama in all, 150-54, headlined by a lengthy drive in the fourth quarter that essentially iced the game for Tennessee. Alabama loses back-to-back games As a result of Saturday's road loss at Tennessee, Alabama has now dropped back-to-back games for the first time since 2013. This is also Alabama's third consecutive loss to Tennessee in Neyland Stadium after defeats in both 2022 and 2024. item.title: Big Cleveland sports day: Browns, Guardians to play back-to-back on Sunday
item.description: Every year, there is a reminder that there is nothing like baseball playoffs (except hockey playoffs, maybe. Full disclosure: hockey and soccer are not my sports, but I do respect them). The NFL playoffs, especially when our Cleveland Browns are in them, are amazing, but there is something different about every pitch mattering for a three-, five-, or seven-game series. With the Cleveland Guardians squaring off with the Tampa Bay Rays, Browns CB Denzel Ward’s involvement (along with many other Cleveland sports names like Cavaliers star Donovan Mitchell ) has been fun to see. Of course, Ward now owning part of the Guardians is a piece of his connection with the team. Sunday will be a big sports day in Cleveland. After the Guards were rained out on Friday night, Game 5 versus the Rays will be held Sunday at 5 PM. Perhaps Ward will join fans who attend the Browns Week 6 matchup with the Baltimore Ravens at 1 PM by hightailing up to Progressive Field (still The Jake to many of us) as quickly as possible for Game 5. The Guardians currently have a 2-1 lead in the ALCS with Game 4’s first pitch at 8 PM on Saturday night. item.title: Aqib Talib unloads on Ryan Fitzpatrick’s rant about Bo Nix: ‘You suck, bro!’
item.description: BOULDER, COLORADO - NOVEMBER 29: Former NFL football cornerback Aqib Talib looks on from the sideline prior to the game between the Colorado Buffaloes and Oklahoma State Cowboys at Folsom Field on November 29, 2024 in Boulder, Colorado. (Photo by Andrew Wevers/Getty Images) | Getty Images Former Denver Broncos cornerback Aqib Talib had some choice words for Ryan Fitzpatrick after he said Bo Nix is disrespectful to the quarterback position with his play against the Seattle Seahawks this week. Talib absolutely eviscerated Fitzpatrick’s comments and I am here for it. Aqib Talib responds to Ryan Fitzpatrick's rant about Bo Nix after the Broncos victory over the Seahawks on TNF Tell em @AqibTalib21 pic.twitter.com/A0ilMh3sBX — MileHighReport (@MileHighReport) October 17, 2026 Zack Kelberman posted the full transcript of this clip on X and it is a line-by-line takedown of TNF’s talking head: “ You are disrespectful to the quarterback position ’cause you suck. Period. … We’re talking about a guy [Fitzpatrick] who played for nine different teams in 17 years. ’Cause ain’t nobody want his ass. We’re talking about a guy who only played for a team for more than two years once. That’s Buffalo. And his record as a starter in Buffalo was 19-35. That’s f*cking suck. “A guy who played 17 years, 147 starts, and never sniffed a playoff game. He never touched the playoffs ever. That’s disrespectful to the quarterback position. “You suck. You suck, bro. “We’re talking about a guy who got 169 interceptions, more interceptions than he has starts. How can a quarterback of his caliber talk about what is disrespectful to the quarterback position? Nobody’s worried about what Fitzpatrick said. Nobody was worried about playing against you. You suck.” Talib is probably the best former-player covering the Broncos in 2026. He gives it straight, but he also defends the team without feeding into the fan overreactions. And hey, I’m certainly one to overreact during and immediately after games. So I appreciate the straight-talk Talib dishes for fans sometimes too. At the end of the day, the Broncos are 4-2 and right where they hoped to be after those first six brutal games on their schedule. Sean Payton and Bo Nix will figure this out and the team is winning while they are.

item.description: ALLENDALE - Grand Valley State football coach Scott Wooster knows the margin for error is zero the rest of the season. item.title: Europe is a blast – but more a curse than a blessing if you are not a Premier League super-club I Jonathan Wilson
item.description: The four Premier League clubs playing in the lesser continental competitions face each other on Sunday – but three are struggling domestically The sun shone. The temperature was in the high 20s. There was a mood of great conviviality. If you were struggling with the official allocation, it turned out you could just email the president of Torreense and he’d sort you out. Were these “Nuno-tickets” real? It turned out they were. Not only that, but you could sit anywhere you wanted in a stadium too big for the game and, if you happened to have gravitated to the comfortable hospitality seating at the back of the lower tier, the beer was inexplicably free. Locals in Leiria seemed bewildered but could hardly have been more accommodating. A beer pump had been installed outside a patisserie on the Praça Francisco Rodrigues Lobo, whose owner soon found fans happy to help stack empty barrels if that facilitated the free flow of Sagres. “There was a meeting at the town hall to explain these are not hooligans,” said the owner of a radical leftist flammkuchen restaurant between the square and the cathedral. “They told us the club comes from the labour movement and I found that very interesting.” And how had she found the fans? “Noisy, but with a quirky sense of humour.” Continue reading...

item.title: Houthi conflict casts shadow as Saudi Arabia scales back sporting pipe dreams
item.description: A match delayed by missile attack warnings is not what Cristiano Ronaldo and co signed up for but it’s the new reality; the Saudi sporting juggernaut is stalling Cristiano Ronaldo grabbed the scarf in the colours of the Saudi Arabian flag and waved it at the sparse but enthusiastic crowd, who responded with rapturous cheers. It was a gesture of defiance rather than a victory salute, encapsulating the Saudi equivalent of “Keep calm and carry on”. Monday night’s Asian Champions League Elite game between Al-Nassr and the Uzbek side Neftchi Fergana had ended with a 3-1 win for the Saudi club coached by Ange Postecoglou, with Ronaldo, supported by Sadio Mané, scoring, the smattering of star names indicative of the lure of the Saudi Pro League. Yet this isn’t quite how Ronaldo and co would have anticipated life in Riyadh. The meagre attendance aside, Monday’s game was delayed by a threat of missile attacks from Yemen’s Houthi rebels. A safety warning issued 15 minutes before kick-off came two days after 13 people died and more than 300 were wounded by Houthi strikes on Riyadh’s King Khalid international airport. item.title: James McClean: ‘Wearing the poppy was just never going to happen’
item.description: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” Continue reading...

item.description: Pundits regularly criticise teams for not running enough but is there a link between distance covered and results? By Opta Analyst It was like clockwork. Speaking on Sky Sports, Jamie Redknapp said: “There’s a pattern I don’t really like when I watch teams, and that’s when – and the stats don’t lie – the other team runs more than you. In the Premier League right now, I feel there are a couple of non-negotiables: you’ve got to run more than the other team if you want to win, or at least get close enough that it doesn’t make that much of a difference. item.title: Football Daily | Guardiola returns to Manchester as City spin into dizzy mess against PSG
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! It is quite funny that PSG felt like the good guys at the Etihad Stadium but if we briefly detach ourselves from the notion that the European champions’ own sportswashing and cashsplashing has also done immeasurable damage to the beautiful game, then their 4-2 Bigger Cup shellacking of Manchester City was pure cinema, baby! I was stunned at reading the comments in support of Manchester City keeping their trophies, coming out of the mouth of their Bigger Cup rivals at PSG (yesterday’s Quote of the Day). Given the example of the organisers of the Tour de Lance … sorry, the Tour de France, this kind of ‘keep the awards you won’ stuff might get him sent to the Bastille. Or consider Formula One. They’ve got all kinds of rules about driver behaviour on the racetrack, and additional rules about what the crew can and cannot do to your car. Cars get inspected before each race, and there are also mandatory post-race inspections for every car. You might drive your car first across the line to the cheers of the crowd, but if the post-race inspection discovered that you cheated in how your team designed your vehicle, your memory of crossing the line is all you get to keep. Think about that for a minute. If the Premier League and Fifa cannot clear the bar for morals in sport set by the UCI and FIA, that says a lot. And none of it good” – Peter Rehwaldt. My friend Bernard grew up in Coventry. And as a boy he thought the team was called ‘Coventry City Nil’. I would get out more, but I’m a Manchester United fan” – Brendan Hughes. item.description: Former Manchester City player is coming out of retirement at 40 to play one match for ambitious Supreme Sha Tin Hong Kong, China (as is the official football name), has long tried to follow the advice of Han Solo in Return of the Jedi: keeping their distance from China while trying not to look like they are keeping their distance. It is all about maintaining an independent football association and the trappings and privilege that come with it. There was some talk a few years ago about getting a Hong Kong team in the Chinese Super League, when the spending was in full flow, and although that did not happen the local Premier League has belatedly got in on the act – kind of. This glittering city is not known as a football hotbed but has a long history in the sport that started when it was a British colony and has continued since it became a special administrative region of China in 1997. George Best, Peter Shilton, Arie Haan, Bobby Moore, Diego Forlán, Nicky Butt, René van de Kerkhof, Tony Morley, Gordon McQueen and Craig Foster have played in the territory and soon David Silva will too. item.description: Manchester City unrepentant in victory, Spurs make progress of a sort and Noni Madueke meets the moment The manner of Manchester City’s victory at Liverpool was an article of both vindication and vilification. item.title: Why we’re stuck with a Premier League in the clutches of the global mega-rich | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: There’s little prospect of the model changing in a country that welcomes wealthy international owners with open arms Football, the world’s most popular sport, played by laws drawn up in London in 1863. The Premier League is the UK’s greatest soft power export. Premier League clubs are owned by a deputy prime minister of Abu Dhabi, the public investment fund of Saudi Arabia, a billionaire based in Monaco for tax reasons and a disappointing assortment of investors and private equity funds. And what, really, could be more British than that? Football truly is the national game. What the Manchester City case has exposed is just how difficult it is to regulate some of the richest and most powerful bodies in the world. While the wait for the verdict was frustrating, it was perhaps unavoidable given the possibility of legal objection at every turn when a leaked email from City’s in-house lawyer during Uefa’s action against the club had threatened to “ spend 30 million on the 50 best lawyers in the world to sue them for the next 10 years”. You didn’t get that with Albert Alexander Sr or Peter Swales. Continue reading...

item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17. item.title: Ousmane Dembélé quietly becomes the main man after long journey to the top
item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...
